Summary.Name: DeepCORO-CTO
Summary.Description: DeepCORO-CLIP based imaging J-CTO scorer for chronic total occlusions on coronary angiography. From up to 10 videos per study it predicts, for each of the three major coronary arteries (LAD, RCA, LCx), the four morphological J-CTO components (blunt/flush stump, calcification at the occlusion, bending > 45°, occlusion length ≥ 20 mm) and an aggregate imaging J-CTO score clamped to [0, 4]. The artery with the highest predicted score is reported as the CTO artery. This is not the classic Morino J-CTO score (0–5): the fifth point for a previously failed crossing attempt is not available from imaging and is not predicted.

Mechanism.Outcome: Per-artery (LAD, RCA, LCx) J-CTO morphological component binary classifications plus imaging J-CTO score (0-4) regression; the highest-scoring artery is reported
Mechanism.Output: jcto_blunt_stump, jcto_calcification, jcto_bending_gt45, jcto_occlusion_length_gt20: probabilities after sigmoid for the selected artery; jcto_score: predicted imaging J-CTO score clamped to [0, 4] (excludes prior-failure point), reported both raw and rounded to an integer; ctoArtery and perArtery expose the selected artery and every artery's raw outputs
Mechanism.Target_population: Adults with a chronic total occlusion (CTO) undergoing coronary angiography at MHI
Mechanism.Input_data_source: Coronary diagnostic angiograms (view class inferred from DICOM positioner angles)
Mechanism.Model_type: Deep Learning (MViT video encoder + view-aware multi-instance linear-probing, 15 per-artery heads)

Model.Purpose: Predict morphological J-CTO components and an imaging J-CTO score per artery to support CTO PCI difficulty assessment
Model.Output: Per artery: J-CTO components (blunt stump, calcification, bending > 45°, length ≥ 20 mm) and imaging J-CTO score (0-4); the artery with the highest score is reported

Uses_and_directions.General_use: Research preview for angiogram-based imaging J-CTO scoring (four morphological features only), stratified by artery.
Uses_and_directions.Target_population_and_use_case: Adults with a CTO on coronary angiography. Videos are pooled per study (up to 10) and each video's angiographic view is inferred from the DICOM positioner primary/secondary angles.
Uses_and_directions.Before_using_this_model: Validated on MHI Labelbox-annotated data only (105 held-out studies, 2026-09-21 refresh). Within-artery AUROC for J-CTO score ≥ 3: LAD 0.75 (95% CI 0.55-0.93, n=37), RCA 0.74 (95% CI 0.62-0.85, n=73), LCx 0.56 (95% CI 0.24-0.86, n=20 — not reliable). CTO artery localisation AUROC: LAD 0.86, RCA 0.92, LCx 0.79. Not validated for clinical use outside MHI. Do not treat the predicted score as classic Morino J-CTO (0–5).

Warnings_and_limitations.Image_Quality: Requires diagnostic-quality coronary angiograms that visualise the occluded segment.
Warnings_and_limitations.Number_of_videos: Uses up to 10 videos per study, ordered by SeriesTime; extra videos are ignored. Padded slots are masked out of the pooling.
Warnings_and_limitations.View_inference: Angiographic view class is derived from DICOM PositionerPrimaryAngle/PositionerSecondaryAngle; when angles are missing a padding view embedding is used.
Warnings_and_limitations.Artery_selection: The reported artery is the one with the highest predicted J-CTO score; non-CTO arteries were trained towards 0. Studies with more than one CTO are reported for a single artery only. LCx predictions are based on few training examples and have wide confidence intervals.
Warnings_and_limitations.Score_definition: Predicted jcto_score is an imaging-only morphological score in [0, 4]. Classic J-CTO also awards 1 point for a previously failed attempt; that history item is not modeled here. predictedInteger rounds the regression output to the nearest whole point; componentsAboveThreshold counts binary heads above 0.5 and may differ from the regression score.
Warnings_and_limitations.Confidence_Scores: Component thresholds default to 0.5 on sigmoid probability and are tracked in class_mapping.json. The J-CTO score heads are regression outputs clamped to [0, 4].
